sections.h2: Your options for selling a Kent house
sections.html:
A Kent homeowner has three ways out: hire a listing agent, run the sale personally, or accept an offer from someone who needs no mortgage. Time, effort and price shift with each, so hold them up against your own deadline.

  • Listing with an agent: plan on staging, cleaning and repairs, followed by showings, the buyer's inspection and a lender's sign-off.
  • Selling on your own: price and terms are yours to set, and so are the advertising, contract and closing paperwork.
  • Selling to a cash buyer: nobody underwrites a loan, so the sale moves quicker. Request the figure you would net and set it beside the other two routes.

A building with tenants raises extra questions, covered below, because Kent runs its own rental inspection program.

sections.h2: Kent's three areas and flood history
sections.html:
Kent has three sections. West Hill runs along Interstate 5. The Valley is mostly industrial and commercial, with some medium-density housing and parkland beside the Green River. East Hill is largely residential with retail. Downtown sits on the east side of the valley, about 16 miles from downtown Seattle and downtown Bellevue. Lake Meridian on East Hill is the largest lake, and Clark Lake and Lake Fenwick are ringed by city parks.

The Green River matters to anyone selling in the Valley. Floods from the Green and White rivers troubled the area for decades until Howard A. Hanson Dam went up at Eagle Gorge in 1962. The city keeps a Floodplains page with flood resources and FEMA elevation certificates, plus a Green River flooding information page. If your house is near the river, ask the city for the elevation certificate and floodplain status before a buyer asks.

Kent has 134,871 residents, a hair under the 2020 count of 136,588. Households average 2.84 people, and the median value of an owner-occupied home is $587,800. The jump from 92,411 residents in 2010 came partly from annexing the Panther Lake area in 2010.

sections.h2: Rental housing rules and your sale
sections.html:
These apply to buildings with two or more units. A 2018 city ordinance requires periodic health and safety inspections by a qualified inspector for apartments, townhomes, fourplexes, triplexes and duplexes inside city limits. A standalone house is not on that list. If you own a duplex or small building and plan to sell, the program shapes what a buyer will ask about.

  • Registration: covered rentals register online every year, with a deadline of November 1.
  • Inspection cycle: each property is inspected once every three years. North East Hill, north of James Street, is on the 2026 cycle. West Hill and the Valley, west of Highway 167, are due in 2027, and South East Hill, south of James Street, in 2028.
  • Penalties: owners whose units fail must make repairs and pass reinspection before renewing the multi-family business license. Failure can bring penalty fees and revocation of the license.

For license questions, call 253-856-5200. Ask the city which cycle year your address falls in before you set a closing date, and keep the latest inspection paperwork in your sale file.

sections.h2: What you file and pay at closing
sections.html:
Washington's real estate excise tax is the largest closing item. Sellers usually cover it, and if they do not, the Department of Revenue treats the buyer as responsible. The state charges 1.1 percent of the first $525,000 and 1.28 percent of the slice from there to $1,525,000, and a local rate rides on top.

Passing title by deed takes three things: an excise tax affidavit, the deed and the payment. Skip mailing them to the state, since a misdirected packet can hold up the county filing and trigger penalties and interest. Deliver them to the treasurer in the property's county, King County for Kent, or let escrow file for you. Payment falls due on the sale date, and a month of delay starts penalty and interest.

Kent's Permit Center takes electronic applications by appointment and issues residential permits for additions and alterations, plumbing, re-roofing and mechanical work. The city publishes separate short forms for a residential plumbing permit, which covers replacing fixtures and hot water tanks, for a re-roof, and for mechanical equipment including gas piping. If a previous owner swapped a water heater or replaced a roof, ask the Permit Center whether a permit was pulled, and check the Permit Logs page for issued permits.

Code Enforcement can tell you whether any case is open on your property, so ask before you set a closing date. An open case can slow a sale, and fixing it first usually costs less than negotiating a credit with the buyer afterward. Keep any letters or notices in your sale file.

Commuters use State Route 167 north to Renton and south to Puyallup, and parts of Interstate 5 and State Route 18 lie in the city, with State Route 516 crossing east to west. Kent Station is the hub for Sounder commuter trains to Seattle and Tacoma, plus King County Metro and Sound Transit Express buses, and RapidRide A runs along SR 99 in west Kent. The I Line is scheduled to connect downtown Kent with Renton and Auburn in 2027. Average travel time to work is 30.4 minutes.

Most addresses belong to the Kent School District. Others sit in Federal Way Public Schools, Tahoma, Highline or the Renton School District, so verify yours before the listing goes live.

• Require the price, closing date and every closing cost in writing.
  • Ask the lender for a payoff statement with the exact balance.
  • Find out how the buyer will prove funds and whether an inspection can cancel the deal.
  • Owners of a duplex or small building should pull rental registration and the latest inspection report.
  • Check with the Permit Center on any water heater, roof or remodel you doubt was permitted.
  • Let escrow estimate state and local excise tax so your net is visible.

Someone keeping your tenants will ask for leases and the inspection record, while someone moving in will care more about permits and flood status. With both sets of papers on hand, you can answer either buyer fast.

faqs.q: Does Kent's rental inspection program cover a single-family house?
faqs.a: No. The program covers apartments, townhomes, fourplexes, triplexes and duplexes, each with two or more units. Owners of those buildings register every year by November 1 and have an inspection once every three years.

faqs.q: Where do I file the excise tax affidavit for a Kent sale?
faqs.a: Take it to the treasurer of the county that holds the property, which means King County for Kent, along with the deed and payment. A packet sent to the state by mistake can stall the filing.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my Kent address?
faqs.a: The Kent School District covers most of the city. Pockets belong to Federal Way Public Schools, Tahoma, Highline Public Schools or the Renton district, so look up your exact address.

faqs.q: How far is Kent from Seattle?
faqs.a: Roughly 16 miles from downtown Seattle and downtown Bellevue. Drivers use State Route 167 or Interstate 5, and Sounder trains leave Kent Station for downtown Seattle at peak weekday hours.

faqs.q: Is flood risk a concern for Kent houses?
faqs.a: It can be in the Green River Valley. Howard A. Hanson Dam went up in 1962 after decades of flooding, and the city keeps a Floodplains page with FEMA elevation certificates. Ask the city about floodplain status for your parcel.
